newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds hold nerve ahead of U.S. jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds hold nerve ahead of U.S. jobs.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed lower as hopes of a further easing in monetary policy continued to boost the market.
*U.S. non-farm payrolls for May due later on Friday.
Australian bond yields closed lower as hopes of a further easing in monetary policy continued to boost the market.
Offshore demand and book-squaring ahead of the long holiday weekend prompted a short squeeze in futures, particularly in three-year bonds which ended close to this week's highs.
"The bond rally can continue. Inflation is low, unemployment high and budget surpluses are just around the corner," said economists at Colonial State Bank in their weekly preview.
"The PPI figures on Thursday should help entrench Australia's low inflation status," they added.

The market held its nerve going into the key U.S. non-farm payrolls for May due later on Friday even though dayside traders will not be able to trade again until Tuesday due to Monday's Queen's Brithday holiday. Payrolls are forecast to a rise 221,000 after the 142,000 increase in April, while the unemployment rate is seen rising to 5.0 percent from 4.9 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
A strong labour force report could stir up worries of another tightening by the Federal Reserve, which some local operators believe would prevent any further easings by the Reserve Bank of Australia.

The market's firm tone saw it generally outperform the dollar bloc and the yield curve steepen. The Australian/U.S. 10-year yield spread is nearing key resistance at 65 basis points and where a break could see a move t0 50 basis points, analysts said.
